###  

I don't think the menu is working in my mobile Android/Firefox browser. The tagline text shifts a little but I can't scroll anymore and there's no menu visible. For [https://communique.jdx.dev/](https://communique.jdx.dev/)
I’ll reproduce the Android/Firefox menu behavior, inspect the menu and scroll-lock code in the repo, then implement and verify a focused fix.

content.text: The symptom is consistent with VitePress opening its mobile nav state (which locks page scrolling) while the nav panel itself is positioned or layered off-screen. I found a custom fixed announcement banner that modifies VitePress’s layout offset, so I’m checking that integration against the framework’s mobile nav CSS now.

content.text: I’ve isolated the Firefox-specific cause: the blur effect is applied to `.VPNav`, which is also the containing ancestor of VitePress’s `position: fixed` mobile menu. Firefox treats `backdrop-filter` as a fixed-position containing block, so the menu is laid out against the short nav header and disappears while VitePress still locks body scrolling. I’m moving the blur to the navbar sibling layer so the visual effect remains without trapping the menu.

input.code: const layout = await localTab.playwright.evaluate(() => { const nav = document.querySelector('.VPNav'); const bar = document.querySelector('.VPNavBar'); const screen = document.querySelector('.VPNavScreen'); const rect = screen?.getBoundingClientRect(); return { viewport: { width: innerWidth, height: innerHeight }, navBackdropFilter: nav ? getComputedStyle(nav).backdropFilter : null, barBackdropFilter: bar ? getComputedStyle(bar).backdropFilter : null, screen: rect ? { top: rect.top, right: rect.right, bottom: rect.bottom, left: rect.left, width: rect.width, height: rect.height } : null, bodyOverflow: getComputedStyle(document.body).overflow }; }); nodeRepl.write(JSON.stringify(layout));
input.title: Check menu layout and scroll lock

content.text: The fix is working at a 360×800 viewport: the menu now occupies the full remaining viewport (`top: 64px`, `bottom: 800px`), its links are visible, and only the intended body scroll lock remains. The blur is still present on the navbar, while `.VPNav` no longer creates Firefox’s problematic containing block. I’m packaging this as a review-ready PR from an isolated worktree so none of the existing uncommitted changes are disturbed.
